blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Geometric Relative Positional Encoding has become the primary mechanism for injecting spatial inductive biases into multi-view transformers. Existing designs condition attention on camera-level frustums or ray-marched depth, associating cross-view tokens through the sensor geometry. Such sensor-centric formulations, however, describe only where a token is observed from, leaving the rich surface geometry of the scene region depicted by the token. In this paper, we advocate a shift toward surface-aware positional encoding that explicitly grounds patch tokens in the geometry of physical surfaces. We introduce HRoPE, which represents the local geometry of each patch as a slanted 3D plane, following the slanted support-window assumption of classical multi-view stereo. We inject token-level, plane-induced homographies into attention as relative transformations. This equips the transformer with a geometric prior for rectifying perspective distortions and aligning patch features across viewpoints. Our encoding requires no ground-truth geometry: the plane parameters can be predicted end-to-end under a view-synthesis objective alone, or derived from foundation models. Extensive experiments on RealEstate10K, CO3Dv2, and DL3DV show that our best variant of HRoPE consistently outperforms the evaluated geometric positional encodings for novel view synthesis. Extensive ablations and analysis show the effectiveness of the proposed encoding. Please refer to our project page at: https://gaohchen.github.io/HRoPE

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: The Transformer has become the de facto architecture for recent feed-forward 3D vision ( Wang et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2025 ; Jin et al., 2025 ) . By tokenizing images from multiple viewpoints and exchanging information via attention, these models exhibit strong capabilities in jointly resolving appearance, visibility, and scene geometry. Attention, however, is permutation-equivariant: it operates on unordered sets and is inherently agnostic to the camera poses, metric scales, and epipolar constraints that couple multi-view observations. Consequently, geometric priors must be explicitly injected, either by conditioning token representations directly (e.g., via camera tokens ( Wang et al., 2025 ) or ray maps ( Jin et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2024a ) ) or by imposing epipolar constraints on attention ( He et al., 2020 ; Charatan et al., 2024 ; Ye et al., 2024 ) . Positional encoding (PE) introduces geometric structure directly into attention by modulating pairwise token comparisons.
blocks.zh: "变形金刚"已经成为近代饲料前导3D视野(王等人,2024年;王等人,2025年;龚等人,2025年)的实际架构. 这些模型通过标注多种观点的图像和通过注意力交换信息,显示出在共同解决外观、能见度和场景几何方面的强大能力。 然而,注意力是常态的-等效的:它运行于无序的集合上,对相机的姿势,度量尺度,以及几对多视图观测的顶点限制具有内在的不可知性. 因此,几何前缀必须明确注入,或者直接通过调节符号表示(例如,通过相机表示(Wang等人,2025年)或射线图(Jin等人,2025年;Zhang等人,2024年a年)),或者通过对注意力施加极化限制(He等人,2020年;Charatan等人,2024年;Ye等人,2024年)。 定位编码(PE)通过调制对偶符号比较,将几何结构直接引入了注意.

blocks.en:
While existing PE designs exhibit increasing geometric fidelity by using priors from images, cameras, and rays, they invariably anchor positional information to the sensor.
RoPE extensions ( Su et al., 2024 ) encode 2D intra-view offsets, leaving inter-view transformations implicit ( Weinzaepfel et al., 2023 ; Wang et al., 2024 ) . GTA ( Miyato et al., 2024 ) and CaPE ( Kong et al., 2024 ) inject relative camera extrinsics to achieve invariance to global rigid motions, while PRoPE ( Li et al., 2025 ) generalizes this to the full projection matrix. Ray-based formulations like RayRoPE ( Wu et al., 2026 ) and URoPE ( Xie et al., 2026 ) integrate depth by localizing patches along viewing rays and re-projecting into the query frame. Across this progression, geometry is parameterized via sensor-centric abstractions: an image coordinate, a camera frustum, or a point of ray termination, leaving the rich local surface structure of the underlying scene unmodeled (see Fig. 1 , left and middle).

blocks.en: This limitation is fundamental because multi-view matching does not compare isolated points; it compares local neighborhoods whose appearances are related through surface-induced deformations. A patch in one view and its corresponding patch in another are connected by a warp determined by the underlying surface geometry, and reliable correspondence requires compensating for this warp before comparing visual features. Given the pixel location and camera geometry, depth locates the patch center, while surface orientation additionally determines how its surrounding neighborhood deforms across views. By providing only view or positional information, existing PEs implicitly impose a fronto-parallel assumption on the attention computation mechanism. Although large neural models can learn to compensate for this bias given sufficient training data, doing so compromises efficiency and generalization. We argue that surface orientation is the missing degree of freedom: current PEs capture the zeroth-order position of a patch but neglect the first-order local orientation that dictates its cross-view appearance transformation.
blocks.zh: 这种限制是根本性的,因为多视图匹配并不比较孤立的点数;它比较了其外观通过表面引起的变形而相联的地方街区. 一个视图中的补丁和另一个视图中的相应补丁通过由基础表面几何测定的曲速连接起来,可靠的通信需要先对这种曲速进行补偿,然后再比较视觉特征. 鉴于像素位置和相机几何,深度定位补丁中心,而表面方向则额外决定其周边邻里如何在视图中变形. 通过仅提供视图或位置信息,现有的项目执行单位在注意力计算机制上隐含了前向平行假设. 虽然大型神经模型在训练数据充足的情况下可以学会补偿这种偏差,但这样做会损害效率和通俗化。 我们主张表面方向是缺少自由度:当前的PEs捕捉到一个补丁的零顺序位置,但忽略了决定其交叉视图外观转变的第一顺序局部方向.

blocks.en:
To this end, we present HRoPE , a Homography Relative Positional Encoding that embeds orientation-aware rectification directly into the attention mechanism (Fig. 1 , right). Inspired by the slanted support windows of classical multi-view stereo ( Bleyer et al., 2011 ; Wang et al., 2021a ) , HRoPE anchors a local tangent plane to each patch token. We use the plane normal and distance, together with the camera poses, to define the homography governing cross-view neighborhood deformations. Concretely, we apply a per-patch 3 × 3 3\times 3 transformation block-diagonally to the queries, keys, and values, and incorporate a closed-form inverse into the key projection so that the resulting attention logits depend exclusively on the relative homography between tokens. As we show in Sec. 3.2 and Appendix A.2 , this mechanism acts as an in-attention analogue of computing a matching score only after both neighborhoods have been rectified onto a shared tangent plane. Consequently, whereas prior geometric PEs merely encode where a token is located, HRoPE explicitly models how its underlying surface transforms across views. This formulation offers two compelling advantages. First, HRoPE strictly generalizes point- and ray-based PEs: when a predicted normal aligns with the viewing direction, the induced transformation naturally reduces to the fronto-parallel case. Second, the per-patch transformation parameters can be regressed
from patch features by a lightweight head trained jointly with
the view-synthesis model, using the view-synthesis objective alone.
The head can optionally use pretrained features from
DINOv2 ( Oquab et al., 2024 ) or VGGT ( Wang et al., 2025 ) , without changing the
encoding formulation or training objective.

blocks.en:
We validate HRoPE on feed-forward novel view synthesis (NVS) across the RealEstate10K ( Zhou et al., 2018 ) , CO3Dv2 ( Reizenstein et al., 2021 ) , and DL3DV ( Ling et al., 2024 ) datasets, where it consistently outperforms view-, projection-, and ray-based encodings. Notably, HRoPE surpasses PRoPE on RealEstate10K without ground-truth camera poses, demonstrating that per-patch homography is a stronger prior than view-level projection. Furthermore, our ablations show that this geometry must condition token interactions multiplicatively, injecting the same information as additive features sharply degrades performance. Finally, HRoPE improves generalization to unseen zooms and wider baselines, supporting its role as a geometric inductive bias. Beyond NVS, HRoPE transfers unchanged to a multi-view diffusion model and to the visual tokens of a spatial reasoning MLLM, improving performance on both
tasks (Appendix A.6 ).

我们在跨RealEstate10K(周等人,2018年),CO3Dv2(Reizenstein等人,2021年)和DL3DV(Ling等人,2024年)数据集上验证了HROPE, 其效绩始终超过视图,投影,以及射线编码. 值得注意的是,HROPE在RealEstate10K上超越了PROPE,没有地面真实相机,表明每幅图谱的投影比视平面投影更强. 此外,我们的描述表明,这种几何学必须多重地限制象征性的相互作用,注入与添加剂特征相同的信息,使性能急剧下降。 最后,HROPE改进了通缩到看不见的缩放和更广泛的基线,支持其作为几何导偏的作用. 在NVS之外,HROPE不会改变向多视图传播模型和空间推理的视觉符号MLLM转移,提高了两者的性能

blocks.en: We summarize our main contributions as follows: 1. We formulate the principle of surface-aware positional encoding , positioning local 3D surface geometry as the natural anchor for comparing patch neighborhoods across views. 2. We propose HRoPE , a per-patch relative encoding that uses plane-induced transforms with closed-form inverses to condition attention logits on relative cross-view homographies. 3. We demonstrate consistent improvements over the evaluated geometric positional encodings on multiple NVS benchmarks and under out-of-distribution view settings. Controlled ablations analyze the roles of transformation structure, local geometry, and feature source, supporting the benefit of the homography inductive bias.
blocks.zh: 我们的主要贡献总结如下: 1. 我们制定地表意识定位编码原则,将当地3D地表几何定位为天然锚点,以比较不同观点的补丁区。 2. 我们提出HROPE, 即每平面相对编码,使用平面引起的带有闭式反面的变换,以相对交叉视图同位素作为注意记录的条件。 3. 我们显示,在多个NVS基准和分配外视图设置下,评价的几何位置编码有前后一致的改进。 受控浮雕分析变形结构的作用,局部几何学,以及特征源,支持了图谱诱导偏差的好处.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Geometric PEs encode camera or scene geometry in tokens
and attention. Absolute variants encode Plücker rays ( Sitzmann et al., 2021 ; Sajjadi et al., 2022 ; Jin et al., 2025 ) or 3D positions ( Liu et al., 2022 ) ,
but depend on the chosen world frame. Relative variants extend rotary encodings ( Su et al., 2024 ; Shaw et al., 2018 ) to camera geometry: GTA ( Miyato et al., 2024 ) and
CaPE ( Kong et al., 2024 ) use relative extrinsics, while PRoPE ( Li et al., 2025 ) also includes
intrinsics through projection matrices. Recent methods move from view- to token-level
geometry: RayRoPE ( Wu et al., 2026 ) predicts per-token depth, RoRE ( Griffiths and Dansereau, 2026 ) rotates
features along rays, and URoPE ( Xie et al., 2026 ) projects per-head depth anchors into the
query frame, following epipolar attention ( He et al., 2020 ; Suhail et al., 2022 ) . These encodings describe camera relationships and point- or ray-level geometry. HRoPE adds an explicit local-plane parameterization whose orientation, together with distance and camera geometry, determines a planar neighborhood’s cross-view deformation. This distinguishes surface-conditioned transformations from point localization without requiring the latter to assume fronto-parallel surfaces.

blocks.en:
Multi-view transformers use camera geometry to associate image tokens across
views. Their applications include stereo depth
estimation ( He et al., 2020 ; Yao et al., 2018 ; Gu et al., 2020 ) , camera and structure
recovery ( Wang et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2025 ) , cross-view completion and
matching ( Weinzaepfel et al., 2023 ) , spatial reasoning ( Yang et al., 2025 ; Wu et al., 2025 ) ,
and camera-controlled video and world modeling ( Li et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026 ; Ma et al., 2025 ) ,
as well as novel view synthesis (NVS).
For feed-forward NVS, methods use feature-conditioned
radiance fields ( Yu et al., 2021 ; Wang et al., 2021b ; Chen et al., 2021 ; Trevithick and Yang, 2021 ; Hong et al., 2024 ) ,
predict 3D Gaussians ( Charatan et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2024a ; Zhang et al., 2024a ) , or directly regress
pixels ( Jin et al., 2025 ; Jiang et al., 2025 ) .
We evaluate HRoPE primarily on novel view synthesis using the
LVSM backbone with plane-induced positional encoding.

blocks.en:
Traditional local stereo methods assume constant disparity within
a support window, introducing a fronto-parallel bias on slanted
surfaces ( Bleyer et al., 2011 ) .
Building on randomized correspondence search ( Barnes et al., 2009 ) , PatchMatch Stereo ( Bleyer et al., 2011 ) addresses this limitation by estimating
a local disparity plane at each pixel and evaluating matching costs
over slanted support windows.
More generally, local planar geometry induces a homography that relates
corresponding image neighborhoods across views ( Hartley and Zisserman, 2003 ) .
Learned multi-view stereo methods also use differentiable geometric warping
to compare features under depth hypotheses ( Yao et al., 2018 ; Gu et al., 2020 ; Wang et al., 2021a ) .
HRoPE draws on the principle of using local surface geometry to guide
cross-view matching. It incorporates per-patch, plane-induced transformations
into multi-view attention, bringing the geometric intuition of
slanted-window matching into positional encoding.

blocks.en: HRoPE is a geometric positional encoding that incorporates a per-token surface plane transform. In Sec. 3.1 , we first review how prior work incorporates camera geometry into multi-view attention. Then, in Sec. 3.2 , we introduce the plane-induced transformation and show how it modulates multi-view attention. With consistent camera geometry, the relative transformation exactly maps points on a shared physical plane across views. For independently predicted per-patch parameters, the same algebraic form modulates attention without requiring an exact physical correspondence for every token pair. Finally, Sec. 3.3 details how these per-patch parameters are predicted from image features and presents a calibrated variant that leverages known camera parameters. The overall pipeline of HRoPE is illustrated in Fig. 2 .

Replacing P i \mathrm{P}_{i} with the plane-induced H i \mathrm{H}_{i} from Eq. 1 allows the relative factor to depend on both the local surface geometry and the camera poses. blocks.en: The patch-specific transformation described in Sec. 3.2 is constructed from ( R , 𝐭 , 𝐧 , κ ) (\mathrm{R},\mathbf{t},\mathbf{n},\kappa) . These parameters are predicted by a lightweight regression head that maps patch features to the components of A \mathrm{A} ( 13 13 scalar values in the general case). The input features can be extracted from a predictor trained from scratch (acting as a learnable positional encoding), a pretrained 2D backbone (e.g., DINO), or a 3D-aware backbone (e.g., VGGT). Our primary implementation regresses these parameters from VGGT ( Wang et al., 2025 ) features; VGGT’s pretraining on geometric prediction tasks provides a strong inductive bias for local surface estimation. blocks.en: 4.1 Novel View Synthesis
blocks.zh: 4.1 小说视图合成

blocks.en:
We evaluate HRoPE on novel view synthesis by applying it to the decoder-only LVSM ( Jin et al., 2025 ) architecture. Each model takes two reference views as input and synthesizes a target view. Following PRoPE ( Li et al., 2025 ) , we train downsized LVSM backbone variants ( ∼ \sim 25M parameters) with different positional encoding methods. We train and evaluate the models separately on CO3Dv2 ( Reizenstein et al., 2021 ) , RealEstate10K ( Zhou et al., 2018 ) , and Objaverse ( Deitke et al., 2023 ) , and report PSNR, SSIM ( Wang et al., 2004 ) , and LPIPS ( Zhang et al., 2018 ) .
To evaluate scaling with the number of reference views, we additionally follow the RayZer ( Jiang et al., 2025 ) protocol and train a larger LVSM backbone variant ( ∼ \sim 53M parameters) on DL3DV ( Ling et al., 2024 ) . We evaluate the model with 2 2 , 4 4 , and 8 8 reference views on the held-out DL3DV benchmark.

blocks.en: 4.2 Ablation Studies and Analysis
blocks.zh: 4.2 研究与分析

blocks.en:
We investigate the design and behavior of HRoPE from three perspectives. First, we compare transformation parameterizations and feature sources for parameter prediction (Sec. 4.2.1 ). Second, we examine the contribution and quality of local geometry through a calibrated-camera comparison, qualitative visualizations, and an oracle geometry experiment (Sec. 4.2.2 ).
Finally, we evaluate generalization under shifts in camera intrinsics and view sampling (Sec. 4.2.3 ).
blocks.zh:
我们从三个角度来调查HROPE的设计和行为. 首先,我们比较转换参数化和参数预测的特征源(Sec 4.2.1 )。 其次,我们通过校准-相机比较、定性可视化和甲骨文几何实验(Sec 4.2.2)来审查局部几何的贡献和质量。
最后,我们评价在相机内在变化和视图采样下的一般化(第4.2.3节)。

blocks.en: 4.2.1 Parameterization and Feature Sources
blocks.zh: 4.2.1 参数化和特征源

blocks.en:
Keeping the overall LVSM architecture unchanged, we compare
transformations with different geometric structures and degrees
of freedom: a depth term (“Depth”), a rotation ( SO ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SO}(3) ),
the calibrated P ⋅ F P\!\cdot\!F transformation, a rigid transformation
( SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SE}(3) ), the homography parameterization used by
HRoPE, and an unconstrained 4 × 4 4\times 4 matrix (“Full”).
Fig. 4 (a) compares these variants against the

Whether using a predictor trained from scratch or frozen VGGT
features, HRoPE achieves the highest PSNR among the evaluated
transformations. In both settings, it outperforms the unconstrained 4 × 4 4\times 4 transformation despite using fewer degrees of freedom.
This suggests that the homography structure provides an effective geometric inductive bias without requiring a fully unconstrained transformation. We additionally compare the homography encoding with a 768 768 -dimensional additive encoding constructed from the same VGGT features. The homography formulation performs better despite using the same feature source, indicating that the improvement is not solely due to access to pretrained VGGT features.

blocks.en: We next fix the homography parameterization and vary the feature source used to predict its parameters. We compare a learnable predictor trained from scratch, including DINOv2 ( Oquab et al., 2024 ) , DepthAnything3 ( Lin et al., 2025 ) , VGGT ( Wang et al., 2025 ) , and VGGT- Ω \Omega ( Wang et al., 2026 ) . Fig. 4 (b) shows that the proposed parameterization improves over PRoPE even when its parameters are predicted from scratch or from DINOv2 features. Notably, DINOv2 † retains a 2D architecture, but its features are fine-tuned within VGGT’s 3D pretraining pipeline and therefore acquire implicit 3D awareness, which helps explain their stronger performance than that of off-the-shelf DINOv2. Performance further improves with stronger pretrained feature extractors, with the geometry-aware VGGT backbone achieving the highest PSNR. These results show that the gains of HRoPE do not depend on a particular pretrained backbone, while more informative geometric features provide additional improvements.

blocks.en: Finally, we test whether more accurate, physically grounded parameters further improve HRoPE. We use Aria Synthetic Environments ( Avetisyan et al., 2024 ) , which provides ground-truth depth, surface normals, and camera parameters, and construct the transformation A A in Eq. 5 using either VGGT-predicted parameters or ground-truth geometry. As shown in Table 3 , replacing the VGGT predictions with ground-truth geometry improves PSNR from 28.555 28.555 to 28.751 28.751 , while also improving SSIM and LPIPS. This result suggests that HRoPE benefits from more accurate geometric inputs under the evaluated oracle protocol.

blocks.en: We first evaluate robustness to changes in camera intrinsics by varying the target-camera focal length at test time. Specifically, we scale the focal length from 1 × 1\times to 5 × 5\times its original value, where 1 × 1\times corresponds to the standard evaluation setting. As shown in Fig. 6 , HRoPE maintains strong performance as the zoom factor increases and achieves the lowest LPIPS across the evaluated focal lengths. In contrast, the calibrated P ⋅ F P\!\cdot\!F variant degrades more substantially under large zoom factors.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
In this paper, we investigated local surface geometry as a prior for positional encoding
in multi-view transformers. Inspired by the slanted support windows of
PatchMatch Stereo, we introduced HRoPE, which uses the structure of
plane-induced homographies to parameterize per-patch transformations
and modulate attention through their relative composition.
The transformation parameters are predicted from patch features
and learned jointly with the view-synthesis model.
Experiments on RealEstate10K, CO3Dv2, Objaverse, and DL3DV demonstrate
improved novel view synthesis over the evaluated positional encodings.
Ablations support the contribution of the transformation structure,
with gains observed for predictors trained from scratch and further
improvements from pretrained features. A calibrated extension also
improves PRoPE by incorporating local planar frames while retaining
its camera projections. These findings support local surface geometry
as a useful inductive bias for multi-view attention.

blocks.en: Eq. 16 defines a pixel-to-pixel mapping conditioned on a local plane. In comparison, the relative projection P i ​ P j − 1 P_{i}P_{j}^{-1} used by PRoPE depends only on camera parameters and does not generally determine a unique correspondence between image pixels. A source pixel 𝐱 ~ j \tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j} specifies a viewing ray 𝐗 j = z j ​ K j − 1 ​ 𝐱 ~ j \mathbf{X}_{j}=z_{j}K_{j}^{-1}\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j} , but its depth z j z_{j} remains unknown. For a nonzero camera baseline, this depth ambiguity generally constrains the corresponding pixel in view i i to an epipolar line. Given a plane hypothesis ( 𝐧 j , d j ) (\mathbf{n}_{j},d_{j}) , Eq. 14 determines the depth at the ray–plane intersection, provided that the intersection is finite and lies in front of the source camera. Substituting this depth into the projection equation yields the homography in Eq. 16 , which maps points on the plane between the two views. Unlike the camera-only relative projection used by PRoPE, a local plane resolves the depth ambiguity along a viewing ray and induces a pixel-to-pixel homography on that plane. blocks.en:
We further evaluate how HRoPE enhances the spatial reasoning ability of multimodal LLMs. Visual tokens in these models are indexed only by their 2D raster location within a frame and their ordinal position in the frame sequence, so self-attention has no explicit representation of the 3D geometric relationship between observations of the same surface. Our proposed HRoPE enriches the visual tokens of a pretrained MLLM with
surface-aware positional information and cross-view correspondence cues, while modifying only their positional encoding. Concretely, we build on LLaVA-Video-7B ( Zhang et al., 2024c ) , sampling 32 32 frames per video and processing them with a frozen VGGT ( Wang et al., 2025 ) aggregator in parallel with the model’s native vision tower. From VGGT’s per-patch features, the prediction head described in Sec. 3.3 regresses ( R i , u , 𝐭 i , u , 𝐧 i , u , κ i , u ) (R_{i,u},\mathbf{t}_{i,u},\mathbf{n}_{i,u},\kappa_{i,u}) , which parameterize the per-patch matrix A i , u A_{i,u} in Eq. 5 . We then insert the block-diagonal operator in Eq. 17 into the language model’s self-attention, applying it only to visual tokens in layers L − 10 L\!-\!10 through L − 2 L\!-\!2 of the 28 28 -layer backbone ( L = 28 L=28 ): the geometric halves of each head’s query and key for token ( i , u ) (i,u) are transformed by H i , u ⊤ H_{i,u}^{\top} and H i , u − 1 H_{i,u}^{-1} , respectively, where H i , u = K i ​ A i , u H_{i,u}=K_{i}A_{i,u} , while the remaining halves retain the native rotary encoding. In this way, the visual stream of the MLLM is explicitly conditioned on per-patch surface geometry, while text tokens and the temporal ordering of frames are left unchanged, making HRoPE a strictly additive augmentation to the pretrained VLM. Following VLM-3R ( Fan et al., 2026 ) , we fine-tune the model for 3 epochs on its released VSI-Bench training split, which combines spatial question–answer pairs over ScanNet ( Dai et al., 2017 ) scenes with embodied route-planning instances, while keeping VGGT frozen throughout.

blocks.en: We report the evaluation results on VSI-Bench ( Yang et al., 2025 ) in Table 6 . Our model and the fine-tuned control take 32 32 frames per video as input. For Spatial-MLLM ( Wu et al., 2025 ) and the Qwen2.5VL series ( Bai et al., 2025 ) , we use 16 16 frames as input. For the other open-source methods and GPT-4o ( Hurst et al., 2024 ) , we follow the VSI-Bench evaluation protocol to select the number of input frames (ranging from 8 8 to 32 32 frames). For Gemini-1.5 Pro ( Team et al., 2024 ) , it samples video frames at 1 1 FPS. HRoPE reaches an average of 59.5 59.5 , ahead of every model in the table and 1.8 1.8 points above the same backbone fine-tuned on the identical data without it. The gains concentrate in the categories that require relating a surface across frames, including absolute distance ( + 8.0 +8.0 ), relative direction ( + 7.1 +7.1 ), and route planning ( + 5.7 +5.7 ). Categories answerable from a single frame show smaller changes. This pattern is consistent with the encoding’s emphasis on local surface geometry. The exception is appearance order, which falls 6.9 6.9 points: it is the one purely temporal task in the suite, and HRoPE spends half of each visual token’s head dimension on the plane-induced map, weakening the ordinal cue it depends on. Since the language backbone, the fine-tuning data, and the frame budget are held fixed across the two rows, both the improvements and this regression are attributable solely to the positional encoding. This controlled comparison substantiates our central claim: the plane-induced homography benefits self-attention whenever it must establish correspondence between two observations of the same surface, irrespective of whether those observations are rendered, denoised, or sampled from video.
